newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia crushes record 500,000 T grapes for 97.
newsitem.headline: Australia crushes record 500,000 T grapes for 97.

text.p: Australian winemakers had crushed a record 500,000 tonnes of premium grapes in the 1997 vintage, up around 6.2 percent on last year, preliminary results of an industry survey showed.
The Winemakers' Federation of Australia said on Wednesday the intake of premium reds in 1997 was up 1.7 percent to 211,000 tonnes and whites up 9.7 percent to 290,000 tonnes.
Federation president Stephen Shelmerdine said in a statement the total 1997 vintage was around 800,000 tonnes, down on the 1996 880,000 tonnes record, but still the second highest recorded.
Grapes are harvested between February and May.
Shelmerdine said the drop in the intake of non-premium varietal grapes reflected the industry's growth strategy.
"The domestic and export markets are quality driven and the record premium crush can only boost that performance," he said.
Yields were down in some areas due to seasonal conditions but were offset by a significant A$630 million vineyard planting programme over the past four years of 20,000 hectares, he said.
Chardonnay intake was up 34 percent to 132,000 tonnes, shiraz up 14 percent to 100,000 tonnes, semillon up seven percent to 52,700 tonnes, the federation said.
Cabernet sauvignon intake was down 5.3 percent to 67,000 tonnes, pinot noir down 9.7 percent to 14,600 tonnes, and riesling down 15 percent to 34,300 tonnes, it said.
Intake of the non-premium sultana was down 43 percent to 114,000 tonnes, it said.
The Federation estimates last year's total premium intake at 472,000 tonnes with a breakdown of Australian Bureau of Statistics figures putting the estimate at around 477,000.

Shelmerdine said overall domestic wine consumption was up 5.9 percent to 330 million litres for the 12 months ended April 1997, with white table wine up 6.6 percent and red table wine continuing recent dramatic growth to be up 18.4 percent.
Volume growth in exports was up 24.3 percent to 156 million litres, with value up 31.1 percent to A$595 million, he said.
The federation said the industry was expected to crush 901,000 tonnes in 1998, with 312,000 tonnes of premium whites and 254,000 tonnes of premium reds.
